summary: Exact candidate 6eaf6c1 reproduces the zero-hit counterexamples and contains no runtime correction. The cache safely reuses arbitrary-depth prefixes only when a complete Mamba state is actually owned at that exact depth; producing such a recurrent-plus-convolution checkpoint or replaying recurrent layers independently is outside the current execution path and could not be changed safely without a supported hybrid model.

tests.what_was_measured: Exact candidate suite: 20 passed; notably its short-prefix regression passes by asserting the unresolved zero hit.

Actual MambaRadixCache with GPU-resident indices: depth-3-only n-1 hit=0, exact depth-2 hit=2, arbitrary depth-37 hit=37, and divergence before depth 64 hit=0; nonzero indices matched independent torch.arange references.
Delivery-base actual-cache results matched the exact candidate results.

remaining_limitations: No hybrid-Mamba weights were prepared, so no end-to-end logits, logprobs, or latency were measured. The current backend does not provide a complete arbitrary-depth recurrent-plus-convolution checkpoint for the three-token case, and the scheduler has no path to retain deeper attention KV while replaying recurrent layers. Therefore no runtime source correction or failing-before/passing-after runtime evidence is claimed.
